sources.title: Working with S3 Vectors and vector buckets
supports: S3 Vectors stores vectors in vector indexes inside vector buckets and answers similarity queries, with no infrastructure to provision
Writes to S3 Vectors are strongly consistent
Sub-second latency for infrequent queries and as low as 100 ms for more frequent ones, as described by AWS
Block Public Access is always on for vector buckets
The service namespace is s3vectors

sources.title: S3 Vectors limitations and restrictions
supports: Up to 2 billion vectors per index, dimensions from 1 to 4,096
Up to 2 KB of filterable metadata and 40 KB of total metadata per vector
Up to 500 vectors per PutVectors or DeleteVectors call
Up to 100 results per page of a QueryVectors response
Up to 100 filter constraints per query on an ENHANCED index

sources.title: AWS Regions, endpoints, and quotas for S3 Vectors
supports: S3 Vectors is available in ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo)

sources.title: S3 Vectors metadata filtering
supports: An ENHANCED index applies the metadata filter before the vector search (pre-filtering)
Vector buckets created on or after September 30, 2026 create ENHANCED indexes
On a CLASSIC index a filtered query may return fewer than top K results
The filter operators, including $eq
All metadata is filterable unless declared non-filterable when the index is created

sources.title: S3 Vectors best practices
supports: AWS recommends one vector index per tenant for multi-tenant workloads, with IAM restricting each tenant to its index
Exceeding request rates returns 429 TooManyRequestsException
Hundreds of QueryVectors requests per second per index

sources.title: Creating a vector index in a vector bucket

sources.title: QueryVectors API reference
supports: QueryVectors performs an approximate nearest neighbor search
The request takes indexArn, queryVector, topK, filter, returnMetadata, returnDistance

sources.title: PutVectors API reference

A PutVectors request takes 1 to 500 vectors, each with a key, data and optional metadata

sources.title: DeleteVectors API reference

definition.ja: 文章を、決まった個数の数の並び（ベクトル）に変えたもの。意味の近い文章が近い向きのベクトルになるように、モデルが作る。
definition.en: A text turned into a list of numbers of a fixed length (a vector). A model produces it so that texts with similar meaning get vectors that point in similar directions.

glossary.ja: ベクトルインデックス

definition.ja: ベクトルを保存し、与えたベクトルに近いものを返す入れ物。S3 Vectors では、ベクトルバケットの中に作る。
definition.en: A store that keeps vectors and returns the ones nearest to a vector you give it. In S3 Vectors it lives inside a vector bucket.

definition.ja: 質問に関係する文章を先に検索し、その文章をモデルに渡して答えを書かせる方法。
definition.en: Searching for text related to a question first, then handing that text to a model to write the answer from.

definition.ja: 検索と引用の単位として切り出した、ノートの一部分。この本では 800 文字ごとに、100 文字ずつ重ねて切る。
definition.en: A piece of a note cut out as the unit of search and citation. This book cuts every 800 characters with 100 characters of overlap.

title.ja: 検索: デプロイ済みで、書き込みも検索もない月
title.en: Search: deployed, with no writes and no searches for a month

ja: 1,000 件のノートが索引済みで、パッセージは 1 件あたり平均 2 つ（ベクトル 2,000 本）と仮定
ベクトル 1 本は 4.2 KB と仮定（1,024 次元 × 4 バイト、キー約 30 バイト、メタデータ約 70 バイト）
書き込み、検索、回答はゼロ
DynamoDB の保存量は 25 GB の無料枠の内側（1,000 件 × 約 2 KB）
空のデッドレターキューと、7 日で消えるログは 0
en: Assumed 1,000 indexed notes with 2 passages each on average (2,000 vectors)
Assumed 4.2 KB per vector (1,024 dimensions x 4 bytes, a key of about 30 bytes, about 70 bytes of metadata)
No writes, searches, or answers
DynamoDB storage stays inside its 25 GB free tier (1,000 notes of about 2 KB)
The empty dead-letter queue and logs that expire after 7 days cost nothing

title.ja: 検索: 月に書き込み 1,000 件、検索 10,000 件、回答 1,000 件
title.en: Search: 1,000 writes, 10,000 searches, and 1,000 answers a month

ja: 索引は search-idle と同じ 2,000 本
書き込み 1,000 件。1 件あたりパッセージ 2 つ、1 パッセージ 400 トークンと仮定（日本語の文字とトークンの比は確かめていない）
PutVectors は書き込み 1 件につき 1 回。1 回の最低課金 128 KB が適用されると仮定
検索 10,000 件。問い合わせの埋め込みは 1 件 30 トークンと仮定
1 回の検索で読む所有者のノートは 10 件、約 20 KB（3 読み込みユニット）と仮定
検索のうち 1,000 件が回答まで進む。回答 1 件は入力 2,500 トークン、出力 150 トークンと仮定
Lambda は 256 MB、arm64。検索 0.5 秒、回答 4 秒、索引 1 秒と仮定
ログは 1 件あたり 1 KB と仮定
データ転送と、問い合わせが返すバイト数（1 回 512 KB まで無料）は未算入
en: The same 2,000-vector index as search-idle
1,000 writes, each assumed to be 2 passages of 400 tokens (the ratio of Japanese characters to tokens was not checked)
One PutVectors call per write, each assumed to be billed at the 128 KB minimum
10,000 searches, each query assumed to embed as 30 tokens
Each search assumed to read 10 notes of the owner, about 20 KB (3 read units)
1,000 of the searches go on to an answer, assumed at 2,500 input and 150 output tokens
Lambda at 256 MB on arm64: assumed 0.5 s per search, 4 s per answer, 1 s per indexed write
Assumed 1 KB of logs per request
Data transfer and bytes returned by queries (free up to 512 KB per query) are not included

items.basis: 1,000 PutVectors calls x the 128 KB minimum, in GB
10,000 queries x 2,000 vectors x 4.2 KB, in GB
1,000 writes x 800 tokens + 10,000 queries x 30 tokens, in 1K tokens
1,000 answers x 2,500 input tokens, in 1K tokens
1,000 answers x 150 output tokens, in 1K tokens
1,000 notes of about 2 KB, 2 write units each

note.ja: 9 ファイル、80 件。トークン化と BM25、順位の合わせ込み、パッセージの切り分け、所有者の分離（絞り込みを無視するインデックス、偽の所有者、乱数で作った当たり 200 回）、テーブルとインデックスのずれ、索引の冪等性と削除、バッチの途中の失敗とやり直し、作り直しとストリームの競合、回答の出典と引用、API の入力の上限、S3 Vectors に渡すリクエストの形、スタックのアサーション
note.en: 9 files, 80 tests: tokenizing and BM25, rank fusion, cutting passages, owner separation (an index that ignores the filter, a forged owner, 200 rounds of random hits), table and index out of step, idempotent indexing and deletes, a failure mid-batch and its retry, the race between a rebuild and the stream, sources and citations of an answer, input limits of the API, the shape of requests to S3 Vectors, and stack assertions
Type check of src, infra, test and scripts

summary.ja: 27章のスタックを AWS に一度もデプロイしていない。未確認: cdkd 0.296.28 が AWS::S3Vectors::Index を Cloud Control 経由で作れること、Titan Text Embeddings V2 が東京から呼べて 1,024 次元を返すこと、S3 Vectors の実際の応答がアダプターのスキーマに合うこと、所有者のフィルターつきの問い合わせが通ること、存在しないキーを DeleteVectors に渡したときの振る舞い、DynamoDB Streams の実際のレコードがハンドラーのスキーマに合うこと、失敗したバッチがデッドレターキューに届くこと、function URL 経由で回答が少しずつ届くこと。
summary.en: The chapter 27 stack has never been deployed. Unconfirmed: that cdkd 0.296.28 creates AWS::S3Vectors::Index through Cloud Control, that Titan Text Embeddings V2 can be called from Tokyo and returns 1,024 dimensions, that real S3 Vectors responses fit the adapter's schema, that a query with the owner filter is accepted, what DeleteVectors does with a key that does not exist, that real DynamoDB Streams records fit the handler's schema, that a failed batch reaches the dead-letter queue, and that the answer arrives piece by piece through the function URL.

resume.ja: `vp run search:infra:deploy`、`vp run search:seed`、`vp run search:smoke` の順に実行する。`vp run search:logs -- --indexer` で索引のログを、`vp run search:reindex` で表と索引の差を見る。存在しないキーの削除は、`search:seed` のあとノートを 1 件消し、同じ REMOVE を再配送させる代わりに `search:reindex -- --apply` を 2 回続けて実行して確かめる。最後に `vp run search:infra:destroy`。
resume.en: Run `vp run search:infra:deploy`, `vp run search:seed`, then `vp run search:smoke`. Read the indexer's log with `vp run search:logs -- --indexer` and the difference between table and index with `vp run search:reindex`. To see what deleting a missing key does, delete one note after `search:seed` and run `search:reindex -- --apply` twice in a row. Finish with `vp run search:infra:destroy`.

summary.ja: 意味の検索で「無関係」とみなす距離のしきい値（`MAX_DISTANCE`、0.7）と、パッセージの長さ（800 文字）は、Titan の実際の埋め込みで調整していない。日本語 1 文字が何トークンになるかも測っていない。
summary.en: The distance past which a hit counts as unrelated (`MAX_DISTANCE`, 0.7) and the passage length (800 characters) were not tuned against real Titan embeddings. How many tokens a Japanese character takes was not measured either.

resume.ja: デプロイ後、`search:smoke` と自分のノートで検索し、ログの `embedded` 行の `tokens` と、S3 Vectors が返す距離を見て `examples/27-search/src/search.ts` の `MAX_DISTANCE` を決め直す。
resume.en: After deploying, search with `search:smoke` and with your own notes, read `tokens` in the `embedded` log lines and the distances S3 Vectors returns, and set `MAX_DISTANCE` in `examples/27-search/src/search.ts` again.

summary.ja: OpenSearch Serverless の NextGen コレクションについて、東京リージョンで使えること、東京での OCU 単価が Classic と同じか、ゼロから戻るまでの時間は、開いた一次情報からは確認できなかった。Bedrock のマネージド型ナレッジベースの料金（1 GB あたり月 5 ドル、Retrieve 1,000 回あたり 1 ドル）は料金ページの値で、Price List の東京の行としては見つけていない。
summary.en: For OpenSearch Serverless NextGen collections, availability in Tokyo, whether the Tokyo OCU price equals Classic's, and the time to come back from zero could not be confirmed from the primary sources opened. The Bedrock managed knowledge base prices (USD 5 per GB a month, USD 1 per 1,000 Retrieve calls) are the pricing page's figures and were not found as Tokyo rows in the Price List.

resume.en: Choose Tokyo in the OpenSearch Serverless console and see whether a NextGen collection group can be created. Confirm prices from the bill or from the usage types in Cost Explorer.
